children.game_version: A 'follow the leader' hunt game where children mimic animal movements to the drum beat.

seniors.seated_version: Participants can sit in a circle and use hand-held percussion to mimic the drum beats while performing gentle head sways.
seniors.standing_version: Rhythmic walking in place without the heavy head-dress to protect the neck and spine.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Maintain a constant, moderate tempo rather than the traditional accelerando.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Men use hands to beat drums; women's arm movements are not specifically detailed beyond joining the gathering.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Performed in an open dancing ground; starts as a gathering and moves into a synchronized group display.
movement_profile.partnering: Communal; men and women dance in the same space but have distinct roles.
movement_profile.posture: Upright but dynamic, with significant head and neck movement for men.

signature_moves.description: Men sway and toss their bison-horn head-gears to the rising tempo of the drums.
signature_moves.name: Horn Tossing

signature_moves.description: Choreographed movements that mimic the procedures and spirit of a traditional hunt.
signature_moves.name: Hunting Depiction

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Starts with a steady pulse and builds to a wild, high-energy climax.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid stiff neck movements which may cause injury due to the weight of the head-dress.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Rising tempo with heavy percussive emphasis
music_profile.sound_description: The sound is dominated by the synchronized beating of drums by the male dancers. As the dance progresses, the tempo increases, creating a driving, hypnotic rhythm. The clattering of cowrie shells on the head-dresses adds a high-pitched percussive layer to the deep thrum of the drums.

basic_steps: Men enter the ground beating drums in a steady rhythm
Women join the circle wearing brass fillets and bead necklaces
Dancers begin a rhythmic walk following the drum beat
Men perform 'horn tossing' by swaying the head-dress to the tempo
The group accelerates movement as the drum tempo increases to a 'wild' pace
teaching.formation: Gathering/Circle; men and women join together in a communal dancing ground.
teaching.level_notes: The dance requires significant neck strength for men to manage the heavy bison-horn head-dress.
teaching.rhythm: Accelerando; starts at a moderate pace and rises to a high-intensity tempo.
